articles.title: New study links internet addiction to exhausted physiological stress systems
articles.summary: A new study analyzing human hair samples reveals that severe internet addiction is associated with lower long-term accumulations of the stress hormone cortisol, suggesting the body’s biological stress response may become exhausted over time.

articles.title: East Germans who experienced repression during the GDR show higher distress and systemic inflammation, study finds
articles.summary: Citizens of former East Germany who faced surveillance and harassment still show higher psychological distress and systemic inflammation decades later. A new study reveals how "soft" authoritarian repression leaves a lasting physical and mental mark.

articles.title: Psychedelics reduce bottom-up brain activity in the default mode network
articles.summary: By mapping brain activity like a moving weather system, researchers found that psychedelics consistently reduce the upward flow of sensory information into higher-order brain regions, offering new biological clues into how these drugs alter human consciousness.

articles.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
articles.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab experiments suggest the popular joint supplement may intensify an abnormal sugar-tagging process in the Alzheimer’s brain, although researchers say clinical trials are needed to determine whether it actually causes harm.

articles.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
articles.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms. Researchers say identifying these hidden drivers could prevent unnecessary medication changes and lead to more personalized treatment.

articles.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
articles.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops. The finding suggests that dreaming may require such intense internal processing that neurons consume energy faster than it can be replenished.

articles.title: Neuroscientists shed light on how the brain juggles talking and listening during real conversation
articles.summary: A new study reveals how the human brain processes conversations across different timelines. Researchers found that speaking relies on short-term neural context, while listening requires the brain to integrate information over much longer stretches of time.

articles.title: How adults feel about their ADHD depends heavily on their specific symptoms
articles.summary: A recent study suggests that adults with ADHD who experience hyperactive and impulsive symptoms tend to view their condition more positively. In contrast, those with primarily inattentive symptoms are less likely to see their diagnosis as advantageous.

articles.title: Human breasts might have evolved to keep big-brained infants warm
articles.summary: Unlike other primates, female humans have permanent breasts. Researchers now suggest this unique anatomical trait evolved to provide essential body heat to infants with large, energy-demanding brains.

articles.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
articles.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.
